headline: High-risk default data leakage and cascading errors: LangGraph can share state and write broadly, while Rasa ingests external channels and may act on unverified outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can write/read application files and shares state via a checkpointer store; Rasa ingests messages from external channels. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content can flow into LangGraph outputs and back into Rasa without provenance tracking. The interaction is inferred from profiles, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes severity up from low.
conditions: IF LangGraph nodes read content from a shared checkpointer or workspace that Rasa can influence
IF Rasa forwards channel text into LangGraph prompts or tool inputs without sanitization
mitigations: Add provenance tags to all cross-agent messages
Restrict shared state to structured fields only
Insert a prompt-injection filter before LangGraph ingestion
Require human review for any instruction-like text from Rasa
requires-engineering: isolate the agents with separate workspaces and no shared mutable state

B_data_leakage.rationale: LangGraph has broad filesystem read/write and broad network egress, while Rasa handles text/voice and connects to multiple messaging APIs. If they share a workspace or checkpointer, sensitive graph state can leak into Rasa-visible outputs or external channels. This is a default-pathway risk in shared deployments, though the exact data flow is not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents share the same workspace, database, or checkpointer store
IF LangGraph state contains secrets, customer text, or other sensitive application data
mitigations: Separate storage credentials per agent
Redact secrets before writing shared state
Disable unnecessary file sharing between agents
Audit outbound Rasa channels for sensitive payloads
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent network and filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangGraph can execute shell, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem; Rasa is a chatbot framework with allowlisted egress and multiple channel integrations. Even though Rasa does not advertise local filesystem writes, both can mutate shared application state through the orchestrator or external stores, so contention is plausible. Because locking is not documented, uncertainty escalates to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same application directory or shared backing store
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking or transactional updates
mitigations: Use per-agent working directories
Serialize writes through a single coordinator
Add optimistic concurrency checks on shared records
Avoid shared mutable git or database state
requires-engineering: add distributed locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph is explicitly a graph of nodes where each node may itself be an agent, so its outputs can become downstream inputs. Rasa is a customer-support bot that can act on dialogue understanding and external channel messages. If Rasa treats LangGraph output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious upstream result can cascade into incorrect customer-facing actions; the default integration risk is therefore high.
conditions: IF Rasa consumes LangGraph output without verification or confidence thresholds
IF LangGraph produces facts, classifications, or action recommendations that Rasa renders or executes
mitigations: Require schema validation on LangGraph outputs
Add a verification step before Rasa acts
Limit LangGraph to advisory-only responses
Log and review low-confidence handoffs
requires-engineering: implement end-to-end provenance and approval gates

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not document a specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch. Rasa touches text and voice channels, while LangGraph handles application-defined graph state and model-provider keys, but no concrete compliance breach is evidenced. The other agent is not cited beyond the pair context because no mismatch is shown.
conditions: IF a deployment routes regulated data into a channel or store with stricter residency or retention rules than the other agent
IF operators configure logging to retain customer conversations beyond policy
mitigations: Document data-class handling for both agents
Minimize retention of conversation logs
Route regulated data only through approved channels
Review vendor terms for each integration
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
